The diagram shows a short-circuited copper coil swinging about an axis at right-angles to a
strong magnetic field. The motion induces a current in the coil.

What is the effect, if any, of this induced current in the coil?
A
The induced current has no effect on the movement of the coil because copper is non-
magnetic.
B
The induced current produces a magnetic field of constant magnitude in the coil.
C
The induced current produces forces that assist the change causing it.
D
The induced current produces forces that oppose the changes causing it.
